item.title: Labeling an SCP and determining its Object Class
item.description: Trying to figure out the Object Class for an SCP that sorta contains more than one SCP. I don't really know how to explain it quickly.
item.content:encoded:
Just some notes before I get into it:
1. Not entirely sure I am putting this thread in the right place since I have never posted on here before. If it is in the wrong place, I am sorry and could you please direct me to the right place?
2. I am not looking for a critique on the SCP I am writing. It is extremely unlikely that I will ever post the page for the SCP because I have no confidence and I just like writing these for fun.

I have two questions I need answers and one may answer the other.
Here is the situation. What I am going to refer to as SCP-X is a large sphere-shaped object that can be used to open a dimensional portal. SCP-Y is a sentient being that has come through the portal from the other dimension. SCP-Y is the only known being that has crossed over. The Foundation does not know if there are more beings on the other side because the portal closed again before they could explore it, and they do not know how to reopen it. SCP-Y has no connection to SCP-X aside from coming through the portal opened up by SCP-X. With that in mind, would the two be kept in the same SCP entry?
If the answer is no, then ignore the rest of this. If the answer is yes, I have another question.
SCP-X is considered Safe. Just build a structure around it (since it is too big to move) and it won't do anything. SCP-Y is Euclid. It is a sentient and sapient being that needs the same basic needs as a human. It also does not like to be contained and may try and break out, but none of its abilities really make it any harder to contain than a normal human. If SCP-X and SCP-Y were to be under the same entry, what would the Object Class at the top of the entry be?

Thanks for any help.

item.title: Continuing an old idea of mine
item.description: Wondering if I could continue an old idea of mine without my co-author.
item.content:encoded:
So about a year and a half ago, I got an idea greenlit for an SCP. At the time, I was sort of overwhelmed and I didn't feel I was a good enough writer to actually finish the draft for it by myself, so I reached out and got a co-author. We never really ended up finishing the draft because of personal life for me. On top of that, my co-author disappeared himself and hasn't done anything on the site since the time we got interrupted in July of 2019. I'm currently in the process of trying to contact him, but I don't have very much hope as our only method of communication was this site.

Now it's been a year and a half, so I'm certainly willing to go through the process of being greenlit again. My main question is if I can't contact him, could I continue writing the idea without him? I'm a much better writer so I'm confident I could do it myself, and I'll still keep his name in my posts of course.

Continuity will be drawn from all sources like Tales including “New Job” and “Fear Alone” as well as Tufto 001 proposal and main page articles like SCP-231-7, 999, & 2317. item.title: Quasi-Rewrites
item.description: Viability of unofficial rewrites like SCP-4166.
item.content:encoded:
SCP-4166 began as what was essentially a rewrite of SCP-166. It was posted in a different slot while the original still existed, but used a lot of the same text and described a very similar entity to 166, if not a reinterpretation of the same one. This seems to have been done with the permission of the original author, however, based on the discussion posts.

I am asking because there's an old SCP from Series 1 that seems generally unpopular now but I think has potential. I would like to rewrite it, but it has too many old upvotes to meet the standard rewrite criteria and the original author, as far as I'm aware, is long gone. Could I do something similar to 4166 and post an SCP that is essentially the same thing but modified to tell a different story and fit current writing standards, or is that plagiarism if done without the original author's consent?

item.title: My first SCP article
item.description: I have so many ideas, but which should I pitch first?
item.content:encoded:
I am new and I have been thinking of a few ideas for SCP articles, but now that I have my big shot I don't which one you guys want to see first, so before I head in for the greenlight, does anyone wanna weigh in on which one you want to read that I should pitch first?

Playing with Fire - silly putty like substance that is plasma at room temperature, from Dr. Wondertainment.
Vampire Bodega - mini-mart where everything seems to be free, but actually draws blood from customers, not noticeable unless the customer comes more than twice a week. May be part of Marshall, Carter and Dark.
Cryovampire - cryogenically preserved person who was successfully revived, but now absorbs heat energy. Must be kept in a room heated to 98.6 degrees Farenheit at which point the ambient temperature neutralizes the anomaly, but as soon as it is exposed to lower temperatures it reverts to a savage that freezes anything it touches.
Alzoidian - a cephalopod like alien life form native to the red spot of Jupiter. Exists in symbiosis with a fungus and another species that resembles a manta ray. Still not quite sure how to explain how the foundation even acquired it…
Scapegoats - the cursed goats that carry the sins of the nation of Israel according to an ancient ritual.
Swine Legion - the cursed swine possessed by demons exorcised by Jesus.

SPC-2806: cybernetics for pugilists who lost limbs in shark attacks so that they may once again punch sharks.

item.title: Edit SCP or new tale?
item.description: I have an idea for an original character based around SCP-2806, should I edit the existing article to include him as a new instance or write a tale and reference the article?
item.content:encoded:
I have an idea for a character that I have a lot of confidence in, but I want to make sure I introduce him correctly. First impressions matter, and if I do this wrong, it could be the end for him, and maybe me too.

So the idea is a cyborg, but not really a complex cyborg, actually he just has a cybernetic arm. It's a concept I have worked with a lot, and I feel it could work with SCP-2806. I know I could make up something more original, but that entry felt like it had everything I needed to work with and I want to work with the universe rather than forcing it around me. The long term story is that he ends up in Alpha-9, but not because he's the coolest guy in the room, but because he got into a situation where he got the offer and it was either this or amnestics, and frankly it was enough on the edge the Foundation was cool either way. So the interesting part of the story is that this a guy who's saving the world one skip at a time because he was in the wrong place at the wrong time.

Where I'm at I think it would work to edit the original article adding the new instance to the description, adding a new containment procedure for the new instance, and an interview between the agent and the SCP to get some info on what seperated this guy from all the others that just get the Skywalker protocol. Should I do all that, or just post the interview as it's own tale with a reference to the article?

item.title: Brainstorming - Amber Water
item.content:encoded:
Basically a brainstorming thread for a potential SCP.

The idea behind it involves an SCP that, in its present state at the time of the article, is a tank of amber-colored water. In a solid or liquid state, the water has no special properties other than its unusual color. In a gaseous state, however - particularly a semi-gaseous mist - the water transports whomever travels through it to an oceanic world with no fauna.

Despite this, I'm thinking that the world is very friendly to life - the seas are freshwater, and there's a diverse ecosystem of plant life beneath the surface, some of which are edible and moderately nutritious to humans, despite their alien nature.

The SCP story itself involves an SCP scientist who's sent to investigate the unusual amber cloud hovering about a mile off the coast of Tanzania, when a powerful wind blows it into him before he has time to adjust his course, transporting him to the oceanic world, where he encounters a large sentient cetacean-like creature and a sentient, flying arachnid-like creature. The story itself would explore the backstory of the world, and the interactions of three sentient creatures and how they interact with their environment when they're unequally built for it, and the power dynamic that emerges as a result of their unequal adaptations.

I'm still figuring out the mechanics behind the mist itself, though the fact that it only facilitates transportation as a mist and not in any other state of matter is key to the story's resolution.
